function: Learned time-domain CSI prediction (DDI-LSTM) for a SISO OTFS LEO link from estimated CSI history, Doppler and distance, replacing pilots in the frame's second half (pp. 1, 6).
system: Downlink SISO OTFS, LEO satellite to ground station, 12 GHz, 30 MHz, M=500, Doppler up to 300 kHz, FDD, no RIS (pp. 3-6).
method: DDI-LSTM: LSTM with fully connected multi-step output, supervised, MSE plus Doppler, path-loss, smoothness and PINN loss terms; the OTFS estimator is classical SBL (pp. 6, 10-11).
data_channel: QuaDRiGa time-domain CIRs of a satellite-ground link, 10,000 samples at 0.625 ms, 80/20 split, artificial noise at set SNRs; TLE/SGP4 Doppler and distance inputs (pp. 9-11).
test_conditions: Same QuaDRiGa dataset for training and testing (80/20 split); input lengths 3-25 steps, SNR 10-30 dB, 5-step output; no new scenario or satellite tested (pp. 10, 14).
baselines: Learned predictors: conventional LSTM, Transformer, previous CNN-Transformer (Figs. 14-15, p. 14); SBL estimator versus original 2D off-grid SBL on complexity only (p. 9); no non-learned predictor.
metrics: NMSE of CSI estimation versus frame length and SNR (p. 13); NMSE of prediction versus input length and SNR (p. 14); SIR maps (p. 12).
complexity: DDI-LSTM O(h(T+h)) with h the hidden size (p. 12); SBL estimator O(4*N_nu^2*N*M) per iteration, 20-30% of the original (pp. 6, 9).
q1_support: p. 9: "we generate a simulation dataset for satellite-to-ground link scenarios using the QuaDRiGa" (QuaDRiGa is a listed standard model; the scenario used is not stated).
q2_support: p. 10: "80% for the training set and 20% for the testing set". Same dataset for training and testing; the MEO and GEO extension is only claimed (p. 12: "can be extended to medium Earth orbit (MEO) or geostationary Earth orbit (GEO) satellites through simple online training"), and SNR and input-length sweeps are not new conditions.
q3_support: p. 14: "the Transformer acts as an attention-based baseline to handle long-range dependencies in time-series data". Only learned baselines (LSTM, Transformer, CNN-Transformer) are compared on NMSE; the SBL estimator is compared with the original SBL on complexity only (p. 6) and no non-learned predictor appears.
q4_support: p. 12: "low computational complexity, O(h(T + h)), where h is the hidden layer dimension".
q5_support: p. 9: "we generate a simulation dataset for satellite-to-ground link scenarios using the QuaDRiGa". The authors' own generated dataset; no code or data link anywhere, and TLE and SGP4 only supply orbital parameters.
notes: Included as area 4: the scheme is OTFS channel acquisition for a high-mobility LEO link (p. 1 'two-stage channel acquisition scheme based on orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) modulation'); the pilot-based delay-Doppler estimator LEO-2D-Off-Grid SBL is classical, and the learned part is the DDI-LSTM predictor for the second half of each frame. Specificity order puts area 4 above 6 (LEO link) and 2. Reviewer to confirm: the DDI-LSTM works on time-domain CIRs from QuaDRiGa, not on the delay-Doppler channel (p. 10: 'We do not use the delay-domain CIRs recovered after' OTFS estimation), so reading it as area 2 (channel prediction) would apply the system check, since p. 4 says 'we consider only a single-input single-output (OTFS-SISO) system', and would exclude it; OTFS and NTN works admit single-antenna links, which is why it is kept. q3: the 'previously proposed CNN-Transformer' (p. 14) is probably the authors' earlier paper [51] (p. 15 reference list; p. 11 'Our previous work'), which the text does not state explicitly; the only non-learned comparison is on complexity, not on NMSE. PDF check: the first page holds the title 'Collaborative Method for OTFS Channel Estimation and Prediction Based on LEO Satellite-Ground Link' and DOI 10.1109/TCCN.2025.3618264, which match the DOI of the work.
